findings.message: function mutates contract state or moves value without `require_auth`; an unauthenticated caller may drive changes
findings.remediation: Call `env.current_contract_address().require_auth()` (or `require_auth_for_args`) before any state mutation that affects value.

findings.message: unchecked arithmetic on a likely value quantity; consider `checked_add/sub/mul` to guard against overflow
findings.remediation: Use `checked_add`, `checked_sub`, `checked_mul` on I128/amounts and handle `None` with a revert.

findings.message: possible reentrancy: the function mutates state and makes an external/invoke call without `require_auth`
findings.remediation: Apply a `non_reentrant` guard, move the external call after all state updates, or rely on `require_auth` of the target.

findings.message: external `invoke_contract`/`call_contract` call detected without an adjacent `non_reentrant` guard
findings.remediation: Consider guarding the calling function with `#[non_reentrant]` to prevent reentrant entry.

findings.message: token `.transfer`/`.transfer_from` call with no prior balance/allowance read; the transferred amount is not derived from what this contract actually holds
findings.remediation: Read `env.ledger().balance(...)` (or a stored allowance) first and derive the amount from it, or add a `require_auth`-guarded allowance check before transferring.

findings.message: `panic!` or `unwrap()` on a code path that may be reachable from callers; prefer returning a Result and reverting with a clear error
findings.remediation: Replace panics with `Result` and use `?`/`ensure!` so callers (and the front-end) can handle failures gracefully.
